answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may transact, much like a cedar that only grows tall after seasons of slow, verifiable growth. At dawn of each settlement window, the network samples agents at random and asks them to prove recent useful work; identities without a real history are throttled. Because each fake identity costs a real stake and real time, the ripple of one attacker spawning thousands of clones fades, while honest agents, rooted in reputation earned over many epochs, keep trading cheaply.
